notes: Descriptive comparison, not a fair contest. RESPINOW forecasts were produced in real time from vintage data (the most recent data week was still incomplete and reporting delays had to be handled by the models); Coldfront forecasts here use today's corrected data for all inputs and for the origin week (final-data backtest), which flatters Coldfront. A vintage-based variant is being built separately.

Season 2025/26 was already used once as the untouched test season of Coldfront's own pre-registered protocol (forecasts/backtest/test.json); the model choice and spread factor were tuned on 2023/24 and 2024/25, so 2024/25 is in-sample for the choice of features and spread. These results were not used to change anything.

Alignment of horizon (verified against the files, see alignment): forecast_date is a Thursday in ISO week F; horizon 1 has target_end_date = Sunday of week F, i.e. the week after the last published data week F-1 (the reporting triangle of the clone ends with week F-1 at delay 0). RESPINOW horizon h therefore equals Coldfront horizon h for origin F-1. 816 of 816 rows satisfy this; horizon 0 rows (nowcast of week F-1) are not scored.

Unit conversion: RESPINOW counts / 831.38 (median of weekly count/incidence over 52 weeks 2025-W41..2026-W40; within the window min 831.38, max 831.38, relative range 0.0 %). Over all 731 overlapping weeks the ratio ranges 831.4..831.4. Coldfront values are not scaled. The ratio is practically constant, i.e. RESPINOW's counts are the RKI incidence multiplied by a fixed population (about 83.14 million), so the conversion adds no uncertainty.

Only quantile levels 0.1/0.25/0.5/0.75/0.9 of RESPINOW are used (0.025/0.975 are ignored) so that all models are scored with the same WIS definition as Coldfront (K=2 intervals plus median). This is not the WIS of the RESPINOW-Hub dashboard (7 levels).

Coverage of cells: every model is scored on exactly the same (origin, horizon) cells within a panel. The RESPINOW archive has gaps (summer, weeks between seasons, single missing weeks) and models differ in how long they were submitted, so the strict intersection (panel "all") has 88 cells in season(s) 2024/25; panel "core" drops the models that do not cover every season; the head-to-head panels "vs:<model>" use all cells shared with one model. KIT-simple_nowcast contains nowcasts only (horizons <= 0) and is not compared.

Bootstrap: confidence intervals (ci95) are for the mean WIS difference ensemble minus the other model, in units of incidence per 100k (negative = ensemble better), from a block bootstrap over origin weeks (blocks of 4, 1000 draws, fixed seed). With so few cells they are wide, horizons of one origin are strongly dependent, and the bootstrap cannot account for the choice of panel; seasonsBetter counts at most two seasons.

Actuals: Coldfront's final ARE incidence per 100k (RKI). The variant "respinow_truth" re-scores the same cells against RESPINOW's latest truth divided by the same ratio; it differs only through the ratio and data revisions.
